subject: Stepdown handoff & implementation slate for VitalDX — MAP proposal
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@vitaldx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stepdown handoff & implementation slate for VitalDX — MAP proposal

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff last week. Per our conversation I sketched a concise Mutual Action Plan (attached) to make the handoff and execution less noisy for both teams. High level, the proposal is a three-phase slate:

1) Discovery & acceptance (1 week) — finalize data scope, success metrics, and SSO test accounts. Owner: Sergio (AE) / VitalDX PM.
2) Integration sprint (4 weeks) — SSO, data ingestion pipeline, inference endpoint validation, and smoke testing. Owner: Monica (SRE) / VitalDX Eng.
3) Production validation & ramp (2–4 weeks) — performance baseline, fallback policy, and post-launch runbook. Owner: Marissa (CS) / VitalDX Ops.

Key milestones (dates proposed):
- Tech pre-check (environment + sample inference) — Sep 10, 2026
- Kickoff + MAP sign-off — Sep 14, 2026
- Integration sprint start — Sep 21, 2026
- Production validation window — Oct 19–Nov 2, 2026

Open asks for VitalDX before we lock dates:
- Confirm kickoff owner and a single technical point of contact for pre-checks (email + calendar).
- Decide whether you will take Dedicated capacity or start on Hosted API for the initial integration (we recommend Hosted for faster time-to-value unless you need strict isolation).
- Complete SOC2 questionnaire responses (we can accept the stub for initial sign-off; full packet needed before production).

I attached a compact MAP PDF and an owners spreadsheet so we can edit responsibility rows in-place. Can you confirm availability for the tech pre-check on Sep 10 and a kickoff the week of Sep 14? If those don’t work we’ll propose alternate windows.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth stepdown from AE to CS + SRE.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Park <emily@vitaldx.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: VitalDX Technical <eng-team@vitaldx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stepdown handoff & implementation slate for VitalDX — MAP proposal

Sergio —

Really helpful outline, thank you. A couple quick notes from our side:

- Procurement is still reviewing final terms; they asked if you can share the SOC2 questionnaire ASAP so they can start internal checks. We received the stub you attached but procurement would like the completed items for our security team before production.
- Our engineering lead asked whether we should plan for Dedicated capacity or start on Hosted. For now they prefer Hosted to iterate faster, but would like the option to transition to Dedicated in Q4.
- The kickoff week of Sep 14 is tight for our PMs; could we move the kickoff to Sep 21? A tech pre-check on Sep 17 would work better for our schedule.

Regarding contacts:
- Technical POC: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@vitaldx.com> (backend lead)
- Procurement: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vitaldx.com>

If you can get the SOC2 questionnaire deck to Lisa and the MAP owners sheet updated with the Daniel contact, we’ll confirm on our side and lock Sep 17 for the pre-check.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Park | Head of Product, VitalDX

Looping in a few operational details we’ll need to own post-handoff. I put a quick owners CSV in the attachments and added acceptance criteria rows we should make explicit during the pre-check. Highlights:

- Acceptance criteria (pre-check):
  * Test user SSO works against Okta test org (SRE owner: Monica).
  * Sample ingestion of 10k events with correct schema (Integration owner: VitalDX Eng).
  * Latency baseline: p95 < 350ms on provided sample traffic (Performance: Marissa/CS).

- Runbook & rollbacks: I drafted a one-page runbook for the initial cutover (attached). It contains immediate rollback steps, throttling knobs, and a contact ladder.

Risk callouts for the MAP:
- Data schema drift during ingestion — mitigate with a staging validation job and a diff report run by VitalDX Eng.
- Secrets delivery for staging — prefer KMS-wrapped secrets and ephemeral artifacts rather than long-lived tokens.

Sergio — can you confirm deal id (I see RDW-2345) and whether we should plan to provision a small Dedicated pool if the customer later elects to move? If they start on Hosted we’ll include a migration checklist into the MAP.

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260907_MAP_owners_sheet.csv (owners + acceptance criteria), runbook-stepdown-1p.pdf
